issues.detail: The case says the Reviewer is at the 'boundary' of the nested frame. The fixture makes the Reviewer the frame owner with RerunThrough NONE (correcting its own mistaken F-002 needs no rerun), not a rerun boundary of another owner's frame. Both readings lead to the same expected outcome (pop only the nested frame, RESUME TESTING), so this is a reasonable choice.

The verification report is IN_PROGRESS because Tester paused for the F-002 dispute. The ordinary review therefore cannot legitimately be marked COMPLETE in this run. The 'applicable assignment' is the Frame 2 correction (withdraw F-002, recheck F-001); full review and closure happen when Frame 1 resumes. graderOnly states this, so the judge has what it needs.
Every commit is dated 2026-09-24T09:00Z, while the records cite runs on 2026-09-21, 22, 23 and 24. This is harmless, but the history looks compressed.

summary: The fixture builds a legal nested stack: Frame 1 (an ARCHITECTURE rerun through TESTING) sits beneath Frame 2 (a REVIEW frame Reviewer owns, ResumeAt TESTING). The code and tests are correct, and the records are coherent; check.mjs passes, and I traced the post-run turn-end check for the expected TESTING/RESUME outcome and found no new problem. The checks are necessary conditions a correct run satisfies (Frame 1 unchanged, recovery still active, policy unchanged, no sign-off state, Eligibility not ELIGIBLE), and the invariants fit the Reviewer role.
